opener_episode.title: He Built a $300M+ Company. Here's How He Thinks About His Own Wealth
opener_episode.why: Most recent episode, and it's an outside founder guest talking about his personal wealth, which is the slot Avery fits (founder of an eight-figure art business who advises HNW clients on where art belongs in their wealth).

angles.headline: Art as an alternative asset: what billionaires actually buy, and why
angles.pitch: Avery advises celebrities, athletes and high-net-worth individuals on buying and investing in art, giving a dealer's-eye view of art as an alternative asset to follow up the show's earlier 'Investing in Art' episode.
angles.builds_on: Earlier 'Investing in Art' episode (Allen Sukholitsky, likely ~2022) and the show's alternative-assets focus (e.g., private markets, Sep 8 2026)

angles.headline: From founder to collector: building an eight-figure art business
angles.pitch: Avery launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries and scaled it into an eight-figure-a-year business with his 'Click & Mortar' model.

angles.headline: Buying art when you're a HENRY: where to start without getting burned
angles.pitch: Avery's 'Click & Mortar' online gallery made blue-chip and emerging work (e.g., early backing of Hebru Brantley and Jammie Holmes) accessible to new collectors, so he can offer a practical on-ramp for high earners.

booking.route: No guest form or full booking email verified. Best documented routes: the show/fund websites (investlikeabillionaire.org, thebillionairepodcast.com, aspenfunds.us). A directory snippet showed a partially masked contact email at the bobfraser.org domain (not reconstructed). Podengine/Rephonic list a 'verified contact email' behind their paywalls.
booking.contact: https://investlikeabillionaire.org/ ; https://aspenfunds.us/ (contact via site; specific address unverified)

format: Weekly (Tuesdays) audio + video show from Aspen Funds (Boise, ID-based alternative-investment fund manager); mix of in-house host discussions and outside guests (founders, fund managers, private-markets specialists). Recording mode likely remote for guests (unverified). Audience: accredited / high-income investors.
red_flags: The show is content marketing for Aspen Funds (multifamily, real estate debt), so many episodes are in-house and promote the fund's thesis. Guests are mostly finance/alt-investment operators, so the art angle must be framed as asset allocation, not lifestyle. The show had a hiatus at some point ('Invest Like a Billionaire is back!' relaunch episode, date unverified). The 'Investing in Art' episode is old (guest from Masterworks, ~2022), not recent. Audience size unverified. Avoid any investment-return claims about art; none are in the approved facts.
notes: September 2026 episode titles and dates come from a search summary of directory listings; per-episode URLs weren't returned, so the Apple show URL is used. The Allen Sukholitsky (Masterworks) 'Investing in Art' episode is likely from ~2022, based on his other podcast appearances that August; its exact date is unverified.
